summary: Full brief on 370977908-1, a 279 ppm, 17.09 d SPOC TCE on a Tmag 9.0 F star, promoted from the second list. The main finding is a dip at phase 0.487, as deep as the transit, in all three orbits with data there and at the target's pixels: vet-v3's phase-0.5 check can't see it, LEO-Vetter misses flagging it only on red noise, and if real it makes this an eclipsing binary. TRICERATOPS's no-G blocker is immaterial (the star is TIC 1150965440, T 20.1), so NFPP 0.126 is a would-be fail, yet every star carrying it sits 4 or more sigma from SPOC's difference-image centroid; ground-based photometry at the transit and phase-0.487 times decides both.

findings.claim: A dip at phase 0.487, about as deep as the transit, sits in every orbit with data at that phase (one PDCSAP event, two QLP S103 events) and at the target's pixels; vet-v3's secondary check only looks at phase 0.5, LEO-Vetter's ModShift leaves it unflagged only on its red-noise test, and if it is real it is an eclipsing binary's second eclipse, not this planet.

QLP's S99-S104 timing error (medians under 10 min, single transits up to 35 min; decision 0022) is far below the 5.4 h offset from phase 0.5. QLP S102 and S103 are redder than PDCSAP (red-noise beta 1.84 and 1.60 against 1.04 to 1.31; checks-with-suspect.json red_noise). If real, the eclipses are nearly equal, so a host must reach the required depth at both: TIC 370977897 (8.5", needs 79%) and TIC 370977892 (13.6", 84% to 97%) cannot; TIC 370977918 (11.3", 19%) can (neighbours.csv). What decides it: ground-based photometry at predicted phase-0.487 times (signal t0 1603.0924, P 17.091442, t0 + (n + 0.4867) P) on the target and the neighbours within 1'. A QLP redelivery of S102 and S103, or an independent FFI extraction, would test the two S103 events. No TESS sector is scheduled (checks.json upcoming_sectors empty).

F1 reads the rules correctly, and a hold is the right rating under the brief and decision 0028. I checked each rule claim.

It hands any-phase secondaries to LEO-Vetter's ModShift in the dossier, and the brief's planet lens names ModShift as the test for "an eccentric secondary away from phase 0.5". The offset to phase 0.4867 is 0.227 d, so checks.json's secondary pass at -0.1 sigma tells us nothing about this dip.

(2) "Unflagged only on its red-noise test" matches the rule. leo_vetter/thresholds.py secondary() returns MS4 & (MS5 | MS6) & ~albedo, and criteria/triage-v1.toml [leo] sets MS4 = 0, MS5 = -1, MS6 = -1. I fed it $TRIAGE_RUN/evidence/370977908-1.json leo_flux.evidence.metrics (output in /tmp/t13/370977908-1/refute-F1-rules/rules.txt):
- MS4 = 5.1186/1.6232 - 5.0085 = -1.855, so it fails.
- MS5 = -0.239 and MS6 = -0.025, so both pass.
- The albedo clause is false (albedo 259.7 is not below 1, and dep_sec 267 ppm is not below 0.1 x 342 ppm), so the secondary is not excused as a planet's.
- With Fred = 1, MS4 = +0.110 and the secondary is flagged. Fred is the only thing keeping it clear.

(3) Decision 0031's first cause, the planet's own occultation, is ruled out. 0031 bounds it at 15.2 ppm or less at albedo 1.0, against 267 to 308 ppm here.

(4) Using the S103 QLP events doesn't break a rule.
- Decision 0022 bars the evidence-only vet's outcomes from the call because a timing error of up to 35.25 min can shave depths. It does not forbid reviewer evidence, and the brief tells reviewers to examine S99 to S104.
- The finding argues the timing point correctly: 35 min cannot move a dip 5.4 h.
- Decision 0023 lets dip-existence tests combine both families ("Dilution only makes a dip smaller").
- The phase arithmetic holds: the S65 event sits at phase 0.48671, and S65 to S103 is 63.00001 periods.

(5) The rating fits. The brief and 0028 define hold as "the public data can't decide" plus a named decider, and the finding names ground-based photometry and a QLP redelivery (both on 0028's list) and an independent FFI extraction. It doesn't claim a kill, and the evidence it lays out is mixed:

- SPOC DV s0001-s0065 puts its weak-secondary maximum elsewhere: tce_ws_maxmes 2.57 at -3.33 d, which I confirmed from $SNAP3/raw/SPOC-TCE.
- Only one of the three events is outside the timing-suspect sectors, and S65 holds a second dip of the same size at another phase.

"At the target's pixels" is literal: the 3x3 box, which F3 says can't separate the 8.5" and 11.3" stars. The physics that rules out the 79% and 84-97% hosts under equal eclipses is sound and goes beyond design 4.4's 100% rule without contradicting it.

One minor point that doesn't change the verdict: the predicted-times formula uses the search ephemeris (P 17.091442). Design 4.2 gives M4's predictions to the density-prior fit (P 17.090965 +- 0.00027). Near epoch 160 the two differ by 0.071 d, about 1.7 h against a 4.5 h event.

findings.claim: Both S11 transits sit on momentum dumps, but the signal holds in S38 and S65 without them; it is a low-SNR signal that one held-out season supports.
findings.evidence: Quality bit 32 in S11's FFI pixel series at BTJD 1603.078 and 1620.203, 0.014 and 0.019 d from mid-transit; S11 dumps come every 3.125 d (. ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-vars.sh; . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-vars.sh; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; /tmp/t13/heavy.sh .venv/bin/python /tmp/t13/370977908-1/dumps.py $SECOND2_RUN/tdi/370977908-1/tic370977908 ~/.cache/tess-hunt/lc/370977908.npz). The 2-min light curve has a 16-minute hole at each (1603.068, 1620.194). S38's and S65's four transits have no dump within 1.2 d, except S65 epoch 87 (a dump 0.42 d after, 0.21 d before the orbit gap; events.py). checks.json: sector_depth S11 354 +- 78, S38 293 +- 59, S65 320 +- 73 ppm (p 0.82); holdout predicts S38 at 5.36 sigma (tension 0.09) and is inconclusive only because S11 and S65 are underpowered (expected SNR 3.8 and 3.9 against 4.0). signal_present 8.0 sigma against 7.0; SPOC's MES 7.32 (s0001-s0065) and 7.66 (s0001-s0039), just over 7.1. QLP S102 and S103 give 427 ppm against PDCSAP's 316 (1.2 sigma; checks-with-suspect.json); QLP publishes no CROWDSAP.

findings.claim: No paper, catalogue or ExoFOP entry names the star as a planet host, binary or variable, but the signal is not undetected: two SPOC TCEs and ExoMiner (PC, 0.782) have it, and a claim must credit them.
findings.evidence: checks.json novelty: two SPOC DV TCEs (s0001-s0039 updated 2021-08-31, s0001-s0065 updated 2023-08-05) and four ExoMiner rows; $SECOND2_RUN/second-list.csv: ExoMiner-v2 2-min score 0.782, PC; never a TOI. literature.json search.exofop: no TOI, CTOI, comments, files or imaging. SIMBAD (sim-script query 'HD 133325'): otypes NIR,*; G2/3V; its 12 bibcodes are the 12 ADS hits. No WDS, VSX or Gaia DR3 eclipsing-binary row within 90" (VizieR asu-tsv on B/wds/wds, B/vsx/vsx, I/358/veb at 226.452627 -51.457178). All 12 hits are catalogues. Two of them test binarity and clear it: Kervella et al. 2019 (doi 10.1051/0004-6361/201834371; VizieR J/A+A/623/A72: PMa S/N 0.68, BinG2 0) and its EDR3 update (J/A+A/657/A7: S/N 0.70 and 1.04, no flag), and Brandt 2021 HGCA EDR3 (doi 10.3847/1538-4365/abf93c; J/ApJS/254/42: chi2 0.057, no acceleration). Gaia DR3 (TAP on gaiadr3.gaia_source): RUWE 0.888, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, non_single_star 0. None flagged.

findings.claim: The transit's own shape and density fit a planet on this star, odd and even disagree mildly only in LEO-Vetter's fits with QLP in, and the search's second signal is noise, not an eclipsing-binary partner.
findings.evidence: checks.json: density 0.5 sigma from the TIC's; grazing in 2% of samples, b 0.47 (flat) and 0.66 (prior); Rp 2.64 and 2.71 Earth radii; odd and even 0.76 sigma in PDCSAP (odd 286, even 347 ppm) and 0.2 sigma in QLP (checks-with-suspect.json). Triage's LEO-Vetter on all nine transits leans the other way: odd 389 +- 39 against even 282 +- 44 ppm (1.8 sigma), trapezoid 499 +- 38 against 356 +- 38 (2.7 sigma), b 0.91 +- 0.07. Rank 2 (22.1987 d, ratio 1.30, SDE 9.4; checks.json other_signals) is not at a novelty harmonic: its t0 1613.755 sits 0.12 d after S11's orbit gap ends (1613.637) and its S65 event (66 periods, 3078.87) is the 343 ppm single dip at 3078.84 (events.py), not one of F1's phase-0.487 events.
